bottlenecks.description: CYP2D6 star allele calling remains the single hardest pharmacogenomic computation due to high polymorphism (>100 haplotypes), structural variation (gene deletions, duplications, CYP2D7 hybrid conversions), and short-read alignment ambiguity. No single tool achieves >99% concordance across all allele combinations.
bottlenecks.evidence: Twist et al. 2019 (Stargazer, Genet Med); Numanagić et al. 2018 (Aldy, PMC9977157); CPIC guidelines 2025

bottlenecks.description: EHR integration and clinical decision support (CDS) infrastructure is fragmented. Most healthcare systems lack the technical capability to order, return, and act on genomic test results seamlessly. Genomic data often stored as static PDF reports invisible to CDS.

Polygenic risk score (PRS) portability across ancestry groups is severely limited. European-derived PRS lose 39-73% predictive accuracy in African-ancestry cohorts. Continental African populations represent <1% of GWAS datasets.
bottlenecks.evidence: PMC13301865 (Bridging Ancestry-Stratified Bias); PMC13340549 (PRS in pharmacogenomics)

bottlenecks.description: Regulatory misalignment between FDA, EMA, CPIC, and DPWG creates implementation complexity. Lack of harmonized guidance across agencies and limited actionable pharmacogenomic information in drug labels.
bottlenecks.evidence: EMA multi-stakeholder workshop report (24 Sep 2024); FDA Table of Pharmacogenomic Biomarkers; CPIC 2025 (PMID:40678821)

bottlenecks.description: Clinician education and reimbursement barriers persist. Sparse insurance coverage, variable evidentiary thresholds by payors, and limited post-graduate training programs impede adoption.
bottlenecks.evidence: Smith et al. 2025 (CPT, doi:10.1002/cpt.3736); CPIC member surveys 2012/2024

bottlenecks.description: Scalability of clinical decision support models is limited by finite genetic data capacity. As more actionable variants are recognized and WGS becomes prevalent, current EHR storage and CDS rule capacity may be exceeded.

np_hard_problems.problem: Single Individual SNP Haplotyping (SIH) / Minimum Error Correction (MEC)
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard; APX-hard in the 1-gap case (no PTAS unless P=NP)
current_approaches: Statistical phasing with reference panels (Beagle, Stargazer)
Combinatorial optimization with copy number and SV detection
gaps: Exact solutions scale exponentially with number of variants
Rare allele combinations (<0.1% frequency) remain difficult to phase accurately

np_hard_problems.problem: CYP2D6 Structural Variation and Copy Number Calling
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (ILP solving restricted to pharmacogene models)
current_approaches: Aldy 4: ILP-based combinatorial optimization for CNV and SV detection
Stargazer: paralog-specific copy number from read depths
Cyrius: SV-aware haplotyping (99.3% concordance vs Aldy 82-87%)
Long-read sequencing (PacBio, Oxford Nanopore) for direct phasing
gaps: Short-read NGS cannot resolve hybrid gene-pseudogene rearrangements
No tool achieves >99% concordance across all structural variant types
Reference panels lack diversity for non-European structural alleles

np_hard_problems.problem: Pharmacogenomic Variant Combination Optimization for Clinical Reporting
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (reducible to set cover / combinatorial matching)
current_approaches: PharmCAT Named Allele Matcher: permutation-based matching with CPIC allele definitions
Rule-based expert systems for guideline translation
FHIR Genomics + CDS Hooks for EHR-triggered reporting
gaps: Combinatorial explosion as gene-drug pairs grow (34 genes, 164 drugs in CPIC)
Novel variants not in allele definitions are not considered
Multi-gene interactions (e.g., TPMT+NUDT15 compound metabolizer status) require heuristic approaches

sota_approaches.name: CPIC Guidelines
sota_approaches.description: Evidence-based gene-drug guidelines covering 34 genes and 164 drugs. 28 active guidelines with >10,000 citations and 1.4M views. 85% of PubMed-indexed PGx implementation studies reference CPIC. API supports >80,000 monthly queries.
sota_approaches.citation: Caudle et al. 2025, Clin Pharmacol Ther, doi:10.1002/cpt.70005

sota_approaches.name: DPWG Guidelines
sota_approaches.description: Dutch Pharmacogenetics Working Group guidelines published in European Journal of Human Genetics. Clinical implication score system (essential, potentially beneficial, actionable). Covers CYP2D6, CYP2C19, UGT1A1, and other pharmacogenes.
sota_approaches.citation: Hulshof et al. 2023, Eur J Hum Genet, doi:10.1038/s41431-022-01243-2

sota_approaches.name: PharmCAT
sota_approaches.description: Pharmacogenomic Clinical Annotation Tool. Extracts PGx variants from VCF, infers haplotypes/diplotypes, generates CPIC/DPWG/FDA guideline reports. 188 GitHub stars, MPL-2.0 license. Validated against GeT-RM reference materials.
sota_approaches.citation: Sangkuhl et al. 2020, Clin Pharmacol Ther, 107(1):203-210

sota_approaches.name: Stargazer
sota_approaches.description: CYP2D6 star allele caller from NGS data. Detects SNVs, indels, and structural variants including gene conversions. 99.0% concordant with orthogonal methods. Extended to other pharmacogenes.

sota_approaches.name: Aldy 4
sota_approaches.description: Efficient genotyper and star-allele caller using combinatorial optimization. Supports long reads, novel phasing model, improved CNV and variant calling. Uses ILP solvers for pharmacogene haplotyping.

sota_approaches.name: PRS-PGx-TL
sota_approaches.description: Transfer learning method for polygenic risk score drug response prediction. Jointly models disease GWAS summary statistics and individual-level PGx data. Two-dimensional penalized gradient descent algorithm.

sota_approaches.name: PharmGKB
sota_approaches.description: NIH-funded knowledge base curating impact of genetic variation on drug response. 209 clinical guideline annotations, 1,225 drug label annotations, 5,185 clinical annotations, 264 curated pathways. CC-BY-SA 4.0 license.
sota_approaches.citation: Whirl-Carrillo et al. 2012, Clin Pharmacol Ther; pharmgkb.org

failure_modes.mode: Incorrect star allele calling due to short-read alignment ambiguity in CYP2D6/CYP2D7 homologous regions
failure_modes.mitigation: Use long-read sequencing (PacBio/Oxford Nanopore) for structural variant resolution; ensemble calling with multiple tools (Aldy + Stargazer + Cyrius); manual review of rare allele combinations

failure_modes.mode: Clinical alert fatigue from excessive or low-specificity pharmacogenomic CDS alerts
failure_modes.mitigation: Tiered alert system with CPIC actionability levels; integrate clinical factors with genetics; use FHIR CDS Hooks for context-aware triggering

failure_modes.mode: Ancestry-biased PRS leading to misclassification in underrepresented populations
failure_modes.mitigation: Multi-ancestry GWAS integration (GPS^Mult); ancestry-aware calibration; report uncertainty estimates; avoid clinical use in populations without validation data

failure_modes.mode: EHR data siloing preventing lifetime pharmacogenomic data reuse
failure_modes.mitigation: FHIR Genomics standards adoption; Genomic Archiving and Communication System (GACS); discrete data storage with patient-centric time-independent access

failure_modes.mode: Regulatory misalignment causing inconsistent prescribing recommendations across jurisdictions
failure_modes.mitigation: Harmonization efforts via CIOMS/ICMRA; CPIC-DPWG-FDA alignment workshops; international pharmacogenomic education initiatives

hardware_requirements.minimum: Single-core CPU, 8 GB RAM, 100 GB storage for targeted genotyping panels and PharmCAT analysis
hardware_requirements.recommended: Multi-core CPU (8+ cores), 32 GB RAM, 1 TB NVMe storage, GPU optional for PRS computation and deep learning-based variant calling

scalability_limits.threshold: Current EHR systems can store ~10,000 discrete variants per patient; WGS generates 4-5M variants per genome

scalability_limits.limit: CYP2D6 star allele calling accuracy with short reads
scalability_limits.threshold: Accuracy drops below 95% for structural variants and hybrid gene-pseudogene rearrangements with <100x coverage short-read NGS
European-derived PRS lose 39-73% predictive accuracy in African-ancestry cohorts; continental African populations <1% of GWAS
Current CDS models support limited drug-gene interventions; scaling challenged as actionable variants grow beyond 500 gene-drug pairs
Combinatorial explosion with >100 haplotypes per gene; novel variant combinations not in allele definitions cannot be called
NP-hard; exact solutions scale exponentially with number of variants; practical limit ~50-100 variants per gene region

regulations: FDA Table of Pharmacogenomic Biomarkers in Drug Labeling (395+ drugs as of Sep 2024)
EMA Guideline on Good Pharmacogenomic Practice (EMA/CHMP/718998/2016, effective 2018)
EMA concept paper on revision (EMA/282050/2025, consultation closed Mar 2026)
CLIA/CAP regulations for laboratory-developed pharmacogenomic tests
GDPR (EU) and HIPAA (US) for genomic data protection
challenges: Regulatory misalignment between FDA, EMA, CPIC, and DPWG recommendations
Lack of harmonized international standards for pharmacogenomic test validation
Data privacy concerns with lifelong genomic data storage in EHRs
Equity and access disparities in pharmacogenomic testing across populations
Liability and reimbursement uncertainty for pharmacogenomic-guided prescribing
Ethical considerations for incidental findings in pharmacogenomic testing

cost_tradeoffs.approach: Targeted genotyping panels (e.g., TaqMan assays for CYP2D6, CYP2C19)
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Fast turnaround (hours), low computational burden, well-validated for common variants; misses rare and structural variants
Comprehensive variant detection including structural variants; lifetime reusable data; higher upfront cost but lower per-variant cost

cost_tradeoffs.approach: Preemptive pharmacogenomic testing with EHR integration
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Reduces adverse drug reactions, avoids trial-and-error prescribing; cost-effective over patient lifetime but requires significant upfront investment

cost_tradeoffs.approach: Polygenic risk score computation for drug response
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Captures multi-gene effects beyond single-gene tests; currently limited by ancestry bias and lack of clinical validation

cost_tradeoffs.approach: Cloud-based pharmacogenomic interpretation (e.g., AWS/GCP genomics pipelines)
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Scalable, pay-per-use, no on-premise infrastructure; raises data governance and privacy concerns for cross-border genomic data
